title: Design: Legacy invoice prints title, description and tech story with no labels
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure Legacy invoice layout is on (Settings, then Invoice), so work order 1's invoice prints in the legacy layout.
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with one labor line, line 1, titled "Replace tie rod" with the description "excessive play".
  • Have line 1 completed with the tech story "Both outer ends worn, replaced and aligned", and work order 1 completed and invoiced today as invoice A.
  • Start on work order 1.
custom_steps:
1. Click the Finance tab.
  2. Set the Estimate / Invoice toggle to Invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1's Finance tab opens.

Step 2:

  • Invoice A shows in the legacy layout.
  • Line 1 prints "Replace tie rod" in bold, "excessive play" on the next line and "Both outer ends worn, replaced and aligned" on the line after it, as in the "Legacy invoice" panel of the attached picture of board 1.3.
  • No word such as "Title", "Description", "Tech Story" or "Scope of work" prints in front of any of the three lines.
  • "What are you doing?" and "Why are you doing it?" appear nowhere on the invoice, while the three lines above do.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 15 (14 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks)

  • Key Decisions: “The narrative carries no label either, and "Scope of work" was considered and rejected. The two invoice views disagree about the label and agree about everything else. The legacy view prints the narrative as a plain paragraph under the description with no label. The modern view prints it under a "Scope of work" heading. Both print the title and the description unlabeled, both put the narrative last, and both drop it entirely when it is absent. Printing no label is the only choice that matches what a customer sees in either view. Rejected: "Scope of work", which only half our customers see, and "Tech Story", which is the one label a customer has objected to in writing (SV-6582).”
  • Feature Overview, Out of scope: “The customer-facing estimate, invoice and credit documents. They have never printed either question and are untouched.”

Not yet checked against a build by us: the QA build (sv10130.qa.shopview.com, QuickBooks host qb1.qa.shopview.com) and staging carry this change, and this case has not been run on either.

References from Design

Design canvas "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Pz1Q6BfvreYFpQwVQZPTE6), copy re-read on 27 Oct 2026 (its one change since 13 Oct: the New Line board's "Title *" now reads "Title"): board 1.3 "What reaches QuickBooks". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above where the PRD speaks, and from the board pictures where it is silent about the look.

The "Legacy invoice" and "Modern invoice" panels of board 1.3 draw the printed invoice itself, a screen of ours: compare work order 1's invoice on the Finance tab with them.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • board-1.3-what-reaches-quickbooks.png

The design's own words:

  • “Why the narrative carries no label Because the two invoice views disagree about the label and agree about everything else. Legacy prints the narrative as a plain paragraph under the description with no label at all. Modern prints it under a “Scope of work” heading. Both print the title and the description with no labels, both put the narrative last, and both drop it entirely when it is empty or reads “Tech story missing.” Printing no label is the only choice that matches what a customer sees in either view.”
  • “Legacy invoice Replace tie rod excessive play Both outer ends worn, replaced and aligned”
